text: Duskwither Grounds are located in northeastern Eversong Woods. They are the site of the floating Duskwither Spire but have recently been overrun by arcane creatures. Groundskeeper Wyllithen is charged with maintaining the grounds.
Dust elementals are elemental conglomerates of air and earth which allows them to speak Auran and Terran dialects of Kalimag.

Dwarven Cloth Britches are a quest reward from The Boar Hunter given by Talin Keeneye in Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh.

The Dwarf Captain's Sword is an one-handed sword wielded by dwarf captains and is probably best used for tanking.
Dustfall Robes are a quest reward from Hints of a New Plague?

Dwarfowitz is a dwarf quest giver located at the Sha'tari Base Camp in Terokkar Forest.

At first, this short-barreled rifle appears to be a blunderbuss or long rifle. Only on closer inspection does one realize it has five barrels instead of one large barrel. A clockwork crank and rotating clockwork action act as the trigger for this reciprocating long arm. The dwarven reciprocator is a brutal and intimidating weapon designed for use against charging opponents at close range. This weapon has proven ideal for dwarven tunnel delvers as well, since it can fill a hallway with enough lead to poison any pursuer permanently. Turning the crank once fires a single shot. Dwarf Commoners are dwarves located in Ironforge that only shows up during most holidays. They usually show up in pairs. One can be seen in Violet Rise on the Isle of Thunder.
Dweezel is a tothrezim healer. He is a member of a group of tothrezim debt collectors led by Thathrell, maintained for particularly dangerous debt collections.
Dwarf Spine is a racial PvP token used for the quest Dwarf Spine (quest) in order to receive a Dented Ashmaul Strongbox.
Duskwood Chest is located in a tower in southeast Westfall just west of the river and north of the hills.

Dwarven Homebrew is a token gift item given out by Ironforge non-guard NPCs during the Love is in the Air seasonal event. These are combined into packages which are in turn hierarchically combined with other pledge packages for buffs and rewards. All of the Love is in the Air token gifts are non-functional as regards their name and picture. Dwarven Homebrew is not a functional alcoholic drink item. __NOTOC__

The Dust Covered Chest is located in Karazhan that appears after you win the chess event.
The Dusty Rug is located in Tarren Mill's inn, on the second floor, in the Hillsbrad Foothills.

Dwarven Construction Workers could be found working around one of the Stormwind canals on a project to build a new road to the Stormwind Harbor. They worked with Construction Workers and Underwater Construction Workers under the supervision of Foreman Wick and Mason Goldgild. Goldgild and Wick report to Baros Alexston.
Dustwind Harpies are harpies located in Razorwind Canyon in Durotar.
Dustwind Pillagers are harpies located in Drygulch Ravine in Durotar.

Dust to Dust is the fourth and final installment of the World of Warcraft: Ashbringer comic.
The Dustbringer is a dagger that may be very rarely obtained from fishing in any open water or pool in Northrend. It is a homage to the Ashbringer.
Duskweaver is a cloth uncommon crafted set from the Wrath of the Lich King. It is crafted by Tailoring.

The Dwarven Axeman is a dwarven unit that was meant to appear in the Into the Shadow Web Caverns mission, likely meant to give Baelgun Flamebeard's forces a melee unit. It used the Bandit model as a placeholder and had a distinctly different speaker than the standard rifleman voice. In-game all of the axeman's dialog were eventually attributed to the already-existing riflemen. There is also a a human farm building in To Tame a Land called the Dwarven Axeman. It can only be seen by opening the map file in the World Editor tool of Warcraft III, and is considered an easter egg.
Dustwallow Keys is a region under centaur control. The sands are rich with gold, and the area is densely populated.
The Dustwind is a group of red-plumaged harpies found residing in both the Drygulch Ravine and Razorwind Canyon in Durotar. They have been menacing the Horde's supply caravan routes' safety.
Dustin Vail is a grand master tailoring trainer located at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown. During Death Rising, he defended the grounds.
Dustbelcher Brutes were ogres of the Dustbelcher group found in the Badlands.
__NOTOC__ Dustbelcher Lords were ogres of the Dustbelcher group. They could be found in the southwestern part of the Badlands.
__NOTOC__ Dustbelcher Maulers are ogres of the Dustbelcher group located in the Badlands.

Dustbelcher Wyrmhunters were ogres of the Dustbelcher group found wandering in the Badlands.
The dwarven tossing hammer is an ancient melee weapon, lighter than a warhammer and is perfectly balanced as a throwing weapon.

The dwarven starting experience takes place in Coldridge Valley, in southwestern Dun Morogh, a level 1-20 zone. When freak natural disasters rocked Azeroth just prior to the Cataclysm, dwarven lands were not spared from calamity. A series of quakes tore through areas surrounding Ironforge, reducing settlements to rubble and taking the lives of many innocent dwarves. The quakes roused numerous troggs from their subterranean dwellings and drove the bestial creatures toward the dwarven settlement of Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. The sudden influx of troggs also caused the savage Frostmane trolls to abandon their usual holdings on Shimmer Ridge and encroach upon dwarf-occupied areas. Threatened

Dwarven golems are a type of golem created by dwarves in their own image. The ones in Blackwing Descent were created centuries ago and were considered the dwarves' greatest tactical achievements. They are likely related to the war golems. Some are also in the service of the earthen of Deepholm.
Duskwatcher's Leggings is a quest reward from Wildmane Cleansing.
Dust Bowl Shield is a quest reward from The Good Stuff (quest).
Dust of Disappearance was required for players who were between the levels of 81 to 85 to replace glyphs that they had already learned.
The Dustwallow Impaler is a quest reward from Challenge Overlord Mok'Morokk.
Dustbelcher Silk is looted from Dustbelcher Chests in the Badlands.
Dwarf Slayer is a PvP guild achievement requiring an honorable kill on all Dwarf classes.

A Dwarf Rune Stone is an archaeology keystone. It acts as 12 Dwarf Archaeology Fragments in research on Dwarven archaeology finds that have 'sockets'. They can also be used in Cataclysm dungeons to grant a group wide buff. The buffs available are: *Blackrock Caverns: Grants Dark Iron Contingency Plan, which reduces elemental damage done to you by 5 percent *Stonecore: Grants Might of the Earthen, which reduces physical damage taken by 5 percent. *Grim Batol: Grants Vengeance of the Wildhammer, which is a 5 percent damage increase
Dwarven Baby Socks are a common dwarf archaeology artifact that requires 30 fragments to complete.
Dust, Dust and more Dust! is a guild achievement for Disenchanting 25,000 items, making this currently the only achievement related to disenchanting.
The Dusty Prison Journals can be found in the Cursed Depths in Tol Barad.

Dwarven Infantry are level 18 - 19 elite mobs who can be found in the 7th Legion Base Camp during the Silverpine Forest storyline. Lord Walden orders the Forsaken adventurer to slay Dwarven Infantry in order to find the 7th Legion Battle Plan.
Duskwing Handwraps is a quest reward from Duskwing, Oh How I Hate Thee....
Duskwing Boots are a quest reward from Duskwing, Oh How I Hate Thee....
Dustbone Horrors are level 85 skeletons found in Halls of Origination.
Dustbone Tormentors are skeletons found in the Halls of Origination.
Dwendel is a young redheaded gnome who came with Gelbin Mekkatorque to the meeting in Darnassus. He is said to have a new possible weapon that may be able to fire fifty arrows in a minute.

The Dustback Gorge connects the Krasarang Wilds far below with the elevated terrain of the Valley of the Four Winds, in the shadow of the Serpent's Spine separating the valley from the Dread Wastes in the southwest corner of the zone.

Duumehi is a Broken that can be found in the Crystal Hall of the Exodar; he appears to be weakened or ill: Nus is caring for him and for Ereuso, who is lying not distant from him. During the Battle for the Exodar, he was inside Velen's protective shield, lying.

The Dwarven Slug is provided by Nato Raintree as an objective for Next of Kin. Nato removed the slug from Gann Stonespire, who was injured in a raid on Bael Modan. Nato asks the player to deliver the slug to Gann's next of kin, Alto Stonespire, in Dustwallow Marsh.

The Dwarven Bunker is a large garrison building that gives Alliance players a better chance at quest reward upgrades, Iron Horde Scraps from members of the Iron Horde around Draenor for transmogrification use, and a source of 1 Seal of Tempered Fate per week. The Horde equivalent is the War Mill.

Dwarven Scouts are dwarven scouts found around Frostmane Retreat in Dun Morogh during the Legion Invasions. They could be found injured or being cornered and captured by demons. Saving them as an Alliance adventurer would improve the score of defense against the Legion.
Dwarven Engineers are friendly dwarven engineers that are at the Legion Invasion locations. They are often found working on siege engines at dwarven military camps.

Duvall was a paladin of the Tyr's Guard and the brother of Efrina. At the time of the third invasion of the Burning Legion, Duvall followed his leader Travard and the Argent Crusade forces to kill the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer at Tyr's Fall. When they entered the tomb, the group discovered abominations of the void and had to eliminate them before Travard could begin the ritual to claim the hammer. As they could not perform the ritual without one of the Sparks of Tyr, which was stolen and taken in the depths of the tomb, Duvall followed the group in their descent towards the Grave-Prison of Zakajz. The Dwarf Gronnling was a gronnling companion that was never made available. Its source was listed as "Drop: Your Weapon" during the Warlords beta, which was likely placeholder text. This pet no longer exists in the database, as its NPC ID was later reused by Murkidan.

Dustite is sold by Thistlefir in the Emerald Dream for 800 Seedbloom.

The earthen (sometimes referred to as earthen dwarves or early dwarves) are stony titan-forged beings that were created by the Titanic Keepers to help shape the subterranean regions of the world during the ordering of Azeroth. Succumbing to the curse of flesh, most of the earthen became mortal creatures of flesh and blood known as dwarves. There remains a sizable population of earthen in Deepholm, Uldaman and Ulduar.

Earth elementals are elemental creatures made of the rock, and energy of the earth itself. Their domain on the Elemental Plane is known as Deepholm and the leader of the earth elementals is Therazane. The Stone Lords rule Deepholm under Therazane. Each of their personalities seems to embody a different aspect of earth. Not all earth elementals are minions of the elemental lords and princes, some are minions of the elemental spirits of Outland.
Ealyshia Dewwhisper is a night elf two handed weapon vendor located in the Tradesmen's Terrace in Darnassus. During the Burning of Teldrassil, she was caught in the chaos. She could be saved.
Earthen Guard drops from Baron Kazum, who can be summoned from a Greater Windstone in Silithus.

__NOTOC__ Dwukk is an orc blacksmithing trainer located in Razor Hill in Durotar. During the events of Escalation, Dwukk was captured by the Kor'kron but soon freed by the Darkspear Rebellion. He supported having his steel turned against the Warchief's corrupt soldiers but also reminded the revolutionaries to leave the civilians alone. Earth Shield is shaman class talent. While active, Earth Shield causes the target to receive 20% more healing from the casting shaman, and attacks against the target will consume a charge of the shield to heal them. The spell can only be active on one target at a time, and cannot stack with Lightning Shield or Water Shield.

The Dying Kodo has not much time life on this world and if not already at the Kodo Graveyard (in Desolace), they'll be heading there soon.

EPGP is based on the concept of Effort Points and Gear Points. Effort Points quantify the effort each member put towards the (common) guild goals and Gear Points quantify what each member got back in return. Loot priority is computed as the quotient of the two; priority (PR) is equal to EP/GP. In a sense EPGP is like zero sum, but without all the need to rebalance the system, or impose taxes to give points for other effort put into the guild. Zero sum awards GP/N points to each player for each item dropped (GP the value of the item and N the number of players in the raid) so that the sum of all points for the members of the guild is zero. EPGP on the other hand is by definition self balanced
